findings.finding: On the 2026-06-08 Q1 call Duluth's CFO said 'For the IEEPA tariffs of approximately $12 million paid last year, we have applied for refunds but have not included any potential benefit in the results this quarter or in the full year guidance' - a windfall equal to ~8.7% of the $138M market cap and ~$0.32/share that is carried at zero in the affirmed FY2026 adjusted-EBITDA guide of $28-32M and in the single sell-side estimate of $(0.05), and Duluth's Q2 ended 2026-08-02, i.e. inside the window in which the rest of retail actually booked these refunds.
findings.adversary_note: Every hard fact in this claim checks out in primary sources, and every one of them is public. The CFO quote is verbatim in the 2026-06-08 transcript, which was republished the same day by Motley Fool, Investing.com, The Globe and Mail, Yahoo and AOL, and Investing.com's own summary carried the refund-exclusion at summary level. The arithmetic is right: 38.0M shares x $3.62 = $137.6M, so $12M is 8.7% of cap and $0.316/share, and the sole estimate really is $(0.05). The peer-timing premise is also right and is not obscure -- it is the dominant US retail earnings story of the season. SCOTUS voided the IEEPA tariffs 2026-02-20, CBP opened the CAPE refund portal 2026-04-20, and by Q2 prints Target ($994M), Home Depot ($730M), Williams-Sonoma ($167.8M to COGS), Kohl's (~$150M), Abercrombie (~$100M), Columbia ($78M), YETI ($45.6M) and Bob's ($45.1M) had all booked them, in Fortune, Chain Store Age, WWD and Yahoo Finance. Coresight published a gated piece on 2026-08-27 built on precisely this claim's analytical frame -- 'which retailers and brands are excluding potential future tariff refunds from guidance, leaving the benefits as potential upside?' -- six days before this print. And the price did move on the day the fact became known: DLTH rose 29.82% on 2026-06-08. What is genuinely not out is the join: no DLTH-specific piece I could find sizes the $12M against the market cap, against the $28-32M FY EBITDA guide, or against the $(0.05) estimate, and Coresight does not cover the name. So the fact is published in mainstream aggregator copy and the frame is published in sector research; only the magnitude and the this-quarter inference are undrawn. That is a contested-magnitude 45, not a 20 and not an 85. Two real magnitude offsets keep it from going higher on my side of the argument rather than lower: peers routed only ~79-84% of receipts to earnings (Columbia $78M -> $62M; Bob's $45.1M -> $37.9M COGS + $5.7M inventory + $1.5M interest), and Duluth may elect to exclude a one-time duty credit from the adjusted-EBITDA metric it guides on, in which case the headline the market trades tomorrow carries it at zero exactly as the guide does.

findings.finding: The 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian imports that took DOO from C$93.82 to C$83.67 between 21 and 26 August explicitly does not apply to goods already subject to Section 232 duties - and BRP's snowmobiles and 'the majority of ORV models' have been Section 232 derivative articles at 25% of full value since 6 April 2026, by BRP's own disclosure.
findings.source_date: 2026-08-22 (effective date stated in document; Section 338 took effect 12:01am ET 22 Aug 2026)
findings.adversary_note: Both legs of this syllogism are primary-source public, and were public before the selloff the finding is built on. I rendered the instrument the hunter could not: Proclamation 11048 (FR 2026-07-23) states verbatim 'The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962', and CBP's own CSMS guidance implements it as HTS 9903.03.15 at a 0% additional rate covering 'Articles of aluminum, of steel or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles' - which is precisely the bucket BRP's snowmobiles and majority of ORV models were dropped into by the 6 April 2026 Section 232 derivative amendment. So the legal conclusion is right, and it is not a discovery: at least ten trade-law alerts (White & Case, Holland & Knight, Davis Wright Tremaine, Baker McKenzie, Troutman, Aprio, C.H. Robinson, GHY, Zonos, Morrison Foerster) said 'goods already subject to Section 232 are excluded' between 21 July and 24 August, several of them noting Proclamation 11048 therefore does not reach vehicles at all. Leg two - that snowmobiles and most ORVs carry 25% Section 232 on full value - is BRP's own 14 April press release and was in every wire story and the Globe and Mail. What is nowhere published is the two-step conclusion applied to DOO by name, and the tape ran the other way: DOO closed C$93.82 on 21 Aug and C$83.67 on 26 Aug, and only C$85.90 by 2 Sep, so roughly 8% of the de-rating still stands. That combination - fully published inputs, no published DOO application, contradicting price action - is the one configuration where publication is not dispositive, which is why this is 65 and not 90. Two further discounts: the causal attribution is the hunter's own, and the one piece that looked for a cause found none ('no company announcement, filing or analyst note dated August 25, 2026 was identified that would explain the move'); the 18 Aug +7.74% the finding would want as confirmation is at least as well explained by TD Securities' upgrade to Buy that same day. And Section 338 took effect 22 August - outside the quarter ended 31 July - so it can only reach this print through commentary, not through the reported numbers, competing for airtime with Canada's dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective 8 September and softening North American retail.

findings.finding: BRP has never once mentioned an IEEPA tariff refund - not in the Q1 FY27 call, not in the FY26 financial statements - while Polaris booked US$74m of IEEPA refunds in the exactly-overlapping quarter with ~US$40m more pending, and BRP's own FY26 tariff drag was described as falling 'mainly on PA&A', the Asia-sourced, IEEPA-dutiable and therefore refundable part of its cost base.
findings.adversary_note: The negative claim is correct and I verified it independently: BRP's Q1 FY27 press release (6-K exhibit 99.1, 28 May 2026) contains no mention of IEEPA, tariff refund, duty refund or tariff recovery; the FY26 MD&A (40-F exhibit 99.3) mentions IEEPA nowhere and quantifies no tariff cost at all, saying only 'the unfavourable impacts of global tariffs mainly on PA&A'; and the Q1 FY27 call did not discuss IEEPA or refunds. So the finding's fact pattern holds. What keeps this off a low score is that every ingredient is a headline, not an obscurity: the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on 20 February 2026, a court ordered the government to begin refunding ~$130bn, the CBP refund portal opened 20 April 2026, and the direct comparable - the only other name the same analysts cover - published its exact number in its 28 July release, where the $74m refund was $0.96 of a $1.97 adjusted EPS and led the coverage. Any desk modelling DOO's July quarter has had 'does BRP get a Polaris-style refund' in front of it for five weeks; that question is canvassed even if the answer is not in consensus. Three things cut the size hard. First, the mechanism is much narrower for BRP than for Polaris: BRP's entire tariff problem as it has described it is Section 232, because USMCA-originating goods were carved out of the IEEPA Canada and Mexico orders from 7 March 2025, so BRP's finished vehicles from Valcourt, Juarez and Queretaro plausibly paid no IEEPA duty at all - only the directly-US-entered Asia-sourced PA&A did, and the China portion of that carries Section 301 duties which are not refundable. Second, BRP has never sized its tariff drag, so 'mainly on PA&A' is not a number; against FY26 revenue and a gross-profit line where a $28.5m EV provision was 116bps, a refundable IEEPA slice of C$20-50m is the realistic band, i.e. C$0.25-0.65 of one-time EPS on a C$85.90 share. Third, and least obvious, BRP reports under IFRS: IAS 37 permits recognition of a contingent asset only when realisation is virtually certain, a stricter gate than the US GAAP judgement Polaris made, and the refund process has been widely described as messy and appealable - so BRP can be fully entitled and still disclose rather than book, which would make this a non-event tomorrow.

findings.finding: BRP's model-year 2027 ORV price sheet, revealed with the 17 August product launch, holds price increases near 1% and outright lowers prices on selected Can-Am Commander, Defender and Outlander models while adding factory-installed content - i.e. BRP is absorbing the 25% ad valorem tariff in margin rather than pricing it, and its CAD 200m mitigation plan is overhead and lean initiatives, not price.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (published after BRP's 17 Aug 2026 MY27 reveal; article headline and body describe the MY27 price sheet)
findings.adversary_note: This restates published guidance and a company press release. On the Q1 FY27 call on 28 May 2026 management told the market in terms not to expect price to carry the tariff: 'don't expect any brutal move on pricing', with increases 'less' than low single-digit percentages, to protect competitive positioning - three months before the MY27 price sheet the finding treats as the reveal. The margin arithmetic is also already given: CAD 500-550m gross incremental tariff impact for FY27 (CAD 650-700m annualised), CAD 200m of mitigation, net CAD 3.10-3.60 per share, and revised FY27 guidance of $9.1-9.4bn revenue and $3.00-3.50 normalised EPS. 'Absorbing the tariff in margin rather than pricing it' is not an inference from the price sheet; it is the guidance. The price sheet itself is then BRP's own newswire release of 17 August ('Can-Am Unveils 2027 Side-by-Side and All-Terrain Vehicles', PR Newswire) plus trade coverage that already draws the conclusion - RideApart and SXS Nation describe BRP adding factory-installed content and selectively lowering prices on Commander, Defender and Outlander specifically 'to drive sales and offset the impact of tariffs'. One sub-claim is simply wrong: the CAD 200m plan is not only overhead and lean - the Q1 call lists 'targeted pricing adjustments' and value-chain efficiencies among its components alongside overhead discipline and a CAD 350m/three-year lean programme. Reach is also weak: MY27 ORV shipments begin around August, so this price sheet lands in Q3 FY27 onward and touches the quarter ended 31 July only through outlook commentary, and the Q2 EPS decline of ~$1.60-1.65 was pre-announced on 28 May. The residual 12 is for the possibility that the specific magnitude - near-1% list pricing plus outright cuts plus added free content, against a 25% ad valorem cost - is a worse net price/mix than a consensus that read 'targeted pricing adjustments' more generously.

findings.finding: Petco's Q2 and FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes NO further IEEPA tariff refunds beyond the partial one received in May 2026, yet CBP's CAPE Phase 2 opened 29 June 2026 and BARK - a pet-products importer - booked a reconciliation line item literally labelled 'IEEPA Tariffs Phase II' worth $7.363M in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which sits entirely inside Petco's 3 May - 1 Aug fiscal Q2.
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this is published, and the implication is the single most repeated pattern of the August 2026 retail reporting season. Petco itself disclosed the assumption on 2026-06-03 in its own press release ('the benefit of a partial IEEPA tariff refund received in May 2026, with no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year') and management said on the call that an appeal date was coming and they were being 'prudent' by excluding it - i.e. the company publicly flagged this as an unbooked upside option. CBP's CAPE Phase 2 opening on 2026-06-29 was covered contemporaneously by Thompson Hine, Diaz Trade Law and GHY. And critically, retailers whose fiscal Q2 ended on almost exactly Petco's date (1-2 August) have already reported large IEEPA refunds booked straight into COGS above prior guidance: Home Depot ~$730M ($685M through COGS) as of 2026-08-02, Williams-Sonoma $167.8M reduction of COGS in Q2 FY2026, plus Target, Dollar Tree, Columbia, Carter's, YETI, Bob's and Haverty's - and Fortune ran a feature on Fortune 500 tariff refunds on 2026-08-19. 'A retailer that guided excluding refunds beats because refunds landed in the quarter ending 1 August' is therefore wire copy, not an insight. The genuinely fresh material is narrow: the BARK $7.4M line item labelled 'IEEPA Tariffs Phase II' and the observation that Phase 2's 29 June opening sits inside Petco's 3 May-1 Aug window. That is real and I have not found it applied to WOOF anywhere. Two further discounts: Phase 2's scope is specifically reconciliation-flagged entries with no type-09 filed, and there is no evidence Petco participates in CBP Reconciliation at all - so the mechanism is conditional, not established; and Petco is mostly a reseller of domestically-manufactured branded pet food, so its direct-import IEEPA base is far smaller relative to sales than BARK's or Williams-Sonoma's. I concede the assembly is not published and that it reaches this print; I do not concede that it is unanticipated, because the company told the market the option existed and a dozen comparable retailers have already exercised it in the same fiscal window.

findings.finding: Petco's FY2026 guide is pinned to 'fuel prices remain elevated at approximately those experienced in the first quarter' - fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr) averaged about $4.71/gal diesel on BTS monthlies ($3.72 / $4.92 / $5.50), fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) averaged about $5.20, and diesel was $5.599/gal on 31 Aug with US diesel cracks setting an all-time record above $106/bbl on 1 Sep and record-low seasonal distillate stocks going into heating season - leaving the stated H2 assumption roughly 19% below spot.
findings.adversary_note: The macro half of this is one of the most heavily covered stories of 2026 and the company-specific half looks arithmetically overstated. Diesel at $5.599 on the week of 31 August (up $1.865 y/y), the first-ever $100+ US diesel crack (record ~$102 on 17 August), and distillate stocks at the lowest for the season since the mid-1990s were reported by EIA, OPIS, RBN, DieselNet and FreightWaves - nobody modelling a 1,400-store retailer's H2 in September 2026 is unaware of it, and Petco itself already named 'higher fuel costs' as a Q2 headwind in the 3 June release. The 19% gap is the weak link. Petco's guidance language on the call was 'expects fuel prices to remain at approximately current levels for the remainder of the year' - current as of 3 June, when diesel was roughly $5.35-5.50 (EIA had $5.511 in late April, $5.65-5.67 mid-May, $5.21 on 8 June). Measured against that, spot $5.599 is ~2-4% above the assumption, not 19%. The 19% only appears if you average the fiscal Q1 quarter and let February's $3.72 drag the base down - and Petco's Q1 exit rate was $5.51, not $4.71. Worse for the claim's direction on this specific print: the hunter's own figure of ~$5.20 for fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) is *below* the level assumed at guidance, so fuel was more likely a small tailwind inside the quarter Petco is about to report than a headwind. What remains is a genuine but modest H2 guidance risk from heating season, worth single-digit millions against a $415-430M EBITDA guide.

findings.finding: The two freshest independent pet-category datapoints both landed on 5 August 2026, after Petco last spoke, and both improved with raised guidance - Central Garden & Pet's Pet segment organic net sales +2% for the quarter ended 27 June 2026 with FY non-GAAP EPS raised to '$2.85 or better' from '$2.70 or better', and Freshpet net sales +15.5% to $305.6M with FY net sales growth raised to 10-12% - while Chewy, the market's default category anchor, does not report until 9 September, a week AFTER Petco.
findings.adversary_note: Both datapoints are wire copy from 5 August and both were traded on the day: Freshpet's $305.6M / +15.5% and the raise to 10-12% net sales growth and $210-220M EBITDA moved FRPT ~8%, and Central Garden's raise to '$2.85 or better' from '$2.70 or better' was covered in the release, the transcript and Investing.com's slide note. Pet-category read-across is the most routine thing a WOOF analyst does; asserting it has not been drawn is an assertion about analyst behaviour, not about publication. Three further problems. First, the claim that these are 'the two freshest independent pet-category datapoints' is not right - Zoetis and Elanco's US companion-animal commentary and Tractor Supply's pet/animal category both landed in late July/early August, and Chewy reported Q1 in June. Second, neither peer reads cleanly to Petco: Freshpet's growth is volume-driven distribution and share gain concentrated in grocery/mass, which is as easily a share loss for specialty retail as a tailwind, and Central's Pet segment at +2% organic is a modest supplier print, not a step-change in Petco's own comp. Third, the binding anchor for WOOF's top line is Petco's own 3 June guide of ~+0.3% net sales 'in line with consensus' - consensus is pinned to company guidance, and the market is expecting revenue roughly flat per the 1 September StockStory preview, so a supplier at +2% organic does not move the estimate the print is measured against. Chewy reporting on 9 September is a calendar fact published on Chewy's IR page. What survives is small: a mild positive tilt to a top line the company has already framed.

findings.finding: 19.51M shares are short against a float of only 90.59M - 21.5% of float and 13.46 days to cover on 1.46M average daily volume - and with the option chain unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid) shorts can only cover in the stock, into a name whose last seven prints moved +34.6%, +31.6%, +23.5%, +14.5%, +8.0%, -6.1% and -23.3%.
findings.adversary_note: This is the definition of structural-and-known, and most of it restates the sealed baseline rather than adding to it. Barchart published an article literally titled 'Is a Giant Short Squeeze Brewing in Petco Stock?' in March 2026, syndicated to Yahoo Finance; Seeking Alpha covered 'Petco spikes 28% with insider buying and a high level of short interest in the backdrop'; TipRanks ran 'Growing short/insider interest sends Petco blasting up over 25%'; and the raw figures sit on free retail pages at Fintel, Nasdaq, Benzinga, TheOnlineInvestor and the stockanalysis.com page the hunter cites. Short interest above 15-30% of float has been continuously published on this name for at least six months. The 'shorts can only cover in the stock because the chain is unusable' leg is not new information either - it is baseline field options.status = unusable_chain, atm_spread_frac_of_mid = 1.2 and total_open_interest = 9,117, i.e. the same document the hunter is being judged against. And the seven-print reaction history quoted is verbatim the baseline's history block, whose median absolute move of 23.34% is already this name's expected move. So the claim's content is: this stock has enormous event convexity - which is precisely what the baseline says. It is also directionless: crowded shorts amplify amplitude, they do not tell you the sign, and two of the seven prints were -6.1% and -23.3%. Minor accuracy note: reported short interest varies widely by vendor and date (19.45M/6.8% of shares out on one page, 27.89M/31.0% of float on Benzinga), so the precise 21.5% is not a stable number.

findings.finding: Netskope's Q1 FY27 cash flow statement shows the free-cash-flow reversal that produced the -19% June print was overwhelmingly working capital, not spending: the accounts-receivable collection tailwind shrank to $22.1M from $79.7M a year earlier, accrued compensation drained $43.6M vs $26.5M and deferred revenue $23.0M vs $4.7M - together more than the entire $79.5M year-on-year swing in operating cash flow (-$53.9M vs +$25.6M) - while the non-GAAP operating loss margin was roughly flat at -14.5%, and the fiscal Q2 comp carries no post-year-end collections distortion.
findings.adversary_note: The line items are real and I verified them in the 10-Q, but the *conclusion* the finding draws is management's own published guidance, given the same day the filing landed. On the 2026-06-03 call the CFO said the negative FCF came from an accelerated shift to annual billings that 'shifts cash collections into later periods', called Q1 'the low watermark', guided sequential FCF improvement in Q2, positive quarterly FCF in H2 and a full-year FY27 FCF margin of +2% to +4% — i.e. exactly 'the reversal was collections timing, not spending, and it gets better from here'. The press release itself said the negative FCF 'was in line with guidance'. The flat -14.5% non-GAAP operating margin is likewise the guided range (-14% to -15% for Q2). What is genuinely not drawn out anywhere I could find is the narrower comp-base point: the year-ago fiscal Q1 contained an $79.7M post-fiscal-year-end AR collection surge and a fiscal Q2 comp does not, so the YoY FCF delta should compress mechanically rather than because anything improved. That is worth something, which is why this is 84 and not 95 — but it is a second-order refinement of a first-order thesis the company published three months ago, and the -19% June reaction was the market pricing the FCF story, not missing it.

findings.finding: Palo Alto Networks reported the identical quarter (ended 2026-07-31) after the close on 2026-09-01 - one session before Netskope - with SASE bookings up 40% year on year and record next-generation-security net new ARR of ~$970M, and its $450M of SASE competitive displacement TCV was described as taken from legacy vendors rather than SSE pure-plays.
findings.adversary_note: This is a mega-cap's results released to the wire 24 hours before Netskope prints, and it is the single most-watched read-through in network security. The SASE bookings figure and the competitive-displacement TCV are in Palo Alto's own press release and in PRNewswire, Investing.com and Barchart coverage on 2026-09-01, and every desk covering NTSK writes the SASE read-through the same evening. Two details also cut against the finding as stated: the +40% SASE bookings figure is a *fiscal-year* number in PANW's release, not a quarterly YoY number, and the release says competitive displacements in nearly 100 accounts representing 'more than $400 million' of TCV, not $450M — so the specific framing is at best loosely sourced to a transcript paraphrase. I am not at 90 because the baseline shows no NTSK move around it (run-up 5d -0.3%), so the *implication* for NTSK is arguably still contested rather than expressed in the price; but the underlying facts are wire copy, which is the 70-85 band by definition.

findings.finding: Netskope's live job board carries 143 open requisitions of which 67 are sales-facing (30 with 'Sales' in the title, 14 Regional Sales Manager, 28 Solutions Engineer, 9 Channel), 88 of the 143 were updated in August or September 2026, and a Regional Sales Manager req was updated today, 2026-09-02 - the capacity build management staked its second-half net-new-ARR reacceleration on is still being funded, not quietly frozen.
findings.adversary_note: Nobody publishes Greenhouse req counts, so the dataset is genuinely unpublished — but its entire informational content is 'management's stated plan is still being funded', and that plan is published guidance from 2026-06-03: roughly 50% of quota-carrying reps newly hired or ramping, H1 net new ARR growth explicitly guided 'lower', and the rep build named as 'a meaningful driver of growth in the back half of the year'. Third-party trackers also already publish the aggregate: Revelio/Unify show ~701 active NTSK postings in 2026, +56.8% vs 2025, and individual sales reqs are visible on LinkedIn, Built In and job aggregators. So the finding confirms a widely-told story rather than contradicting it, and confirmation of guidance is close to the top of the scale by the stated anchors. Separately the mechanism barely reaches tonight: open reqs on 2026-09-02 say nothing about the quarter that ended 2026-07-31, and management will reassert the capacity narrative on the call whether or not the reqs exist.

findings.finding: Three months after announcing on 2026-06-03 that CFO Drew Del Matto would retire 'effective upon the start of a successor', no successor has been named: EDGAR shows the only 8-K since is a 2026-07-09 item 5.07 annual-meeting filing, and the company's own board carries no CFO, Controller or Chief Accounting Officer requisition.
findings.adversary_note: The CFO retirement is not obscure: it was in the 2026-06-03 8-K and press release, Investing.com's headline that night was literally 'Netskope tumbles 22% despite Q1 beat on weak FCF, CFO transition', and TD Cowen cut its price target citing the ARR miss and the CFO exit while stating explicitly that they 'would await the appointment of a new CFO'. That last line is the whole finding, published by a covering broker three months ago: the market's stated position is that the successor has not been named and it is waiting. The 8-K/no-successor observation is therefore an absence of news against a known open item, not new information — nobody believes a CFO was hired without an announcement. The supporting evidence is also weak in a way that cuts against the finding: public-company CFO searches run through retained executive-search firms, so the absence of a CFO/Controller requisition on a Greenhouse board is not evidence about the search at all. The retirement is also structured to be non-disruptive — Del Matto stays until a successor starts and will present tonight — so the mechanism into this print is a sentiment overhang already worn.

findings.finding: Netskope's third-party-tracked incident history shows an unusual cluster inside the reported quarter - service impacts at SJC1, SJC2, PVG1/PVG2 and AM2 data centres and to BWAN management plane services in the US region during July 2026, culminating on 2026-07-16 in 'Service Impact to Auth Service and Enterprise browser on all DPs', an authentication failure spanning every data plane.
findings.adversary_note: I concede the publication point: I searched and found no financial-media, sell-side or newswire coverage of the July 2026 incident cluster, and the only sources are third-party status mirrors (isdown.app, StatusGator, SaaSHub) that reflect Netskope's own trust page. That is the 20-40 band — public, but obscure and with the implication drawn nowhere. My number stays low-to-mid rather than very low because (a) the underlying source is the company's own public status page, so it is available to anyone who looks, and (b) the size does not reach this print in any way I can size. Netskope revenue is ratably recognised subscription; a one-day authentication failure on 2026-07-16, two weeks before quarter end, cannot move the reported revenue or ARR for the quarter ended 2026-07-31. Any real economic damage runs through renewal behaviour and NRR at future renewal dates, i.e. FY28, plus immaterial SLA credits. So this is the classic 'real, unpublished, mechanism does not reach the print' case: it belongs in a forward risk note, not in tonight's number, and the option chain is leaning the other way (upside paid, put/call OI 0.48) with no sign anyone is paying for a service-quality shock.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 consensus revenue is $237.99M, roughly 7% below what Methode's own disclosed FY27 building blocks imply for the quarter (Q1 FY26 base of $240.5M, plus the guided data-centre ramp from ~$80M to ~$130M i.e. ~+$12M/quarter, plus North American automotive going from $182M to ~$200M), and the same model was at $238.46M against a $298.1M actual last quarter and $224.57M against a $240.5M actual in the year-ago quarter.
findings.adversary_note: The consensus number itself is the hunter's own published source (MarketBeat/DailyPolitical, 2026-08-31: $(0.27) and $237.985M), and every one of the 'building blocks' it is measured against was disclosed by management on 2026-06-24 and reported the same day: data centre $80M to ~$130M, North American automotive $182M to 'close to $200 million', FY27 sales $1,025-1,075M. So the arithmetic is a re-arrangement of public inputs, not new information. Worse, the arithmetic breaks when you respect the rest of the same disclosure. CFO Kowalchik said on that call 'we expect a lighter first quarter driven by typical seasonality' with sales ramping into a stronger second half. Consensus $238M is 22.7% of the $1,050M guide midpoint, versus Q1 FY26's 23.6% share of FY26's $1,019M actual - i.e. consensus already encodes a lighter-than-normal Q1, exactly as guided. The hunter's ~$257M would put Q1 at 24-25% of the year while H2 is supposed to be stronger, which only fits at or above the very top of the guided range. The building blocks are also gross of the offsets management folded into a +0.6% to +5.5% total-sales guide: EV program roll-offs, Interface weakness, the dataMate divestiture ($16M sale, closed after Q3 FY26) and the Harwood Heights disposal. Finally, the two-quarter 'consensus is 7% low' pattern is cherry-picked - Q2 FY26 revenue beat consensus by 4.6% ($246.9M vs $236.13M) and the stock still fell 10.9% the next day on an EPS miss, and StockStory's own MEI copy states MEI 'has missed Wall Street's revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years'. Revenue versus a four-analyst consensus is demonstrably not this stock's reaction driver; EBITDA and guidance are. Residual novelty: nobody has written up 'this thin consensus sits below the disclosed run-rate', and the calendar's rogue $(0.47) single estimate does show the sell-side print here is unreliable. That is worth something, but not much, and not 7%.

findings.finding: Every external datapoint bearing on Methode's two growth lines post-dates the 25 June guide: hyperscaler 2026 capex was raised across the board in late July (Amazon $200B to $220B, Alphabet $180-190B to $195-205B, Meta narrowed up), and GM raised its own FY26 EBIT guidance by $500M on 21 July while running Flint Assembly six days a week from June on heavy-duty pickup demand - while Methode's data-centre number is built only on existing vendor-managed busbar volume with the 800VDC rack architecture explicitly excluded from guidance by management.
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this is front-page wire copy, and more damagingly, it is the exact narrative the last 24% of this stock's move is made of. Amazon/Alphabet/Meta's 2026 capex raises were the dominant tech story of late July and are the hunter's own CNBC source of 2026-07-28. GM's second 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance raise was a PRNewswire release at 06:30 ET on 2026-07-21 carried by Morningstar, Barchart, Yahoo and TradingView. 'Methode is an AI-datacentre busbar supplier levered to hyperscaler capex' is not a discovery in September 2026 - it is why the stock went from $13.09 to $18.00 on 2026-06-25 (+37.5%) when management first put the $130M datacentre number on the tape, and why Craig-Hallum initiated Buy with a $30 target on 2026-08-25, moving the stock +14.4% in one session. The observation that 800VDC is excluded from guidance is itself a management statement on the 2026-06-24 call ('none of that is in our guide'), reported at the time, so the 'free option' framing is the sell-side's framing, not a discovery. The one thing the finding gets right that is genuinely underdrawn is the timing asymmetry - the guide is dated 25 June and the macro datapoints post-date it - but with the stock up 43% off the 2026-08-24 close of $14.03 and the put skew nonetheless bid at +14.2 vol points, the market is not treating the guide as a ceiling. It is treating it as stale in the same direction the hunter is.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26's headline was inflated by $22.5M of non-recurring customer recoveries recognised as revenue, so adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M on 24.2% gross margin sat on roughly $275.6M of underlying revenue and only single-digit-millions of underlying EBITDA; management said recovery activity is 'largely done' and excluded the remaining balance from FY27 guidance, so this print delivers the year's worst sequential optics - revenue down ~15% and EBITDA down sharply from Q4 - into a stock at a 52-week high.
findings.adversary_note: The $22.5M of customer recoveries is not a detail buried in an exhibit - it is in the second sentence of the company's own 2026-06-24 headline release ('net sales were $298.1 million ... including $22.5 million of customer recoveries') and was repeated in essentially every piece of coverage, including StockTitan, GlobeNewswire, Yahoo, Investing.com and the Motley Fool piece explaining the 40% jump. 'The recovery activity is largely done' is a direct quote from the same call. And the sequential collapse the finding calls 'the year's worst sequential optics' is already the published expectation: consensus of $237.99M against a $298.1M actual is a -20% sequential print that the sell-side has written down, and management pre-announced it as 'a lighter first quarter driven by typical seasonality'. A decline the company guided and the consensus already models is not a surprise; it is the base case. The residual is the second-order point that ex-recoveries EBITDA was only ~$7.9M ($26.9M less the ~$19M management said flowed to earnings), so the sequential EBITDA optic is uglier than the revenue optic - but that adjustment is also published (see MEI-2#0), and it is the same arithmetic. The '52-week high' framing is the only part with real force, and it is the baseline restated: pct_from_52w_high is -3.68 and the put skew is already bid at +14.2 vol points, so the market is paying for the risk that ugly optics into a high gets sold.

findings.finding: Exactly one year ago Methode postponed this same fiscal quarter's release on the scheduled release day - 3 September 2025, having pre-announced 3 September on 21 August 2025 - gave no reason whatsoever in the reschedule notice, and the stock fell 11.4% the following session; it then reported six days later, on 9 September 2025, with a revenue beat ($240.5M vs $224.57M) and an EPS beat (-$0.22 vs -$0.40).
findings.adversary_note: The two anchoring documents are both public company releases from a year ago, and they were wire-distributed: the 2025-08-21 pre-announcement of a 3 September date (Nasdaq press release) and the 2025-09-03 reschedule notice (GlobeNewswire, carried by the Globe and Mail, Manila Times and Yahoo Finance), followed by the 2025-09-09 release with the beat. I confirmed the reschedule notice does indeed give no reason - two sentences, no explanation - so that part of the claim holds. But this is the weakest-mechanism finding in the set on three counts. First, the magnitude is wrong: close-to-close on 2025-09-04 was $7.65 to $7.02, i.e. -8.2%, not -11.4% (Yahoo daily bars). Second, the follow-through cuts against the bear read - the actual 2025-09-09 print produced +12.2% on 2025-09-10, so the pattern the finding documents ends in an up move, and the 'low bar' half of the claim is the same argument as MEI-1#0. Third, and decisively, it is a low-probability tail with a shrinking window: it is 16:10 UTC with the release a few hours away and no 8-K or notice has appeared; last year's notice hit at roughly 20:05 UTC on the scheduled day, so there is residual window, but a single non-recurring precedent with no stated cause and no visible 2026 analogue (no restatement, no auditor change, no material-weakness disclosure I can find) is not a probability the market should be paying much for. Where I concede: the -8.2% reschedule reaction and the +12.2% print reaction are nowhere in this baseline (history.n is 0, a records bug), nobody has written 'watch for a repeat', and the market is genuinely not being shown that base rate. That is why this is not an 80.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M (9.0% margin) versus Q3 FY26's $7.3M (3.1% margin) is a $19.6M sequential jump that is almost exactly the ~$19M of one-time EV customer recoveries management said flowed through to earnings; ex-recoveries Q4 margin was ~2.9%, i.e. flat with Q3, and the FY27 guide of $72-82M adj EBITDA is therefore +47% to +67% off a recovery-adjusted FY26 base of ~$49M, not the +6% to +20% the headline $68.2M comparison implies.
findings.adversary_note: This is the strongest arithmetic in the set and it was published on the day of the guide, by more than one outlet, in a larger version than the hunter's. TipRanks' Q4 FY26 report page, dated 2026-06-24, states the FY27 guide of '$72-82 million (implying a ~7.0-7.6% margin; ~13% growth vs FY2026 and ~82% growth ex-refinements/recoveries)'. Investing.com's coverage of Methode's own Q4 FY26 slide deck puts the same figure at ~51% adjusted EBITDA growth excluding FY26 portfolio actions and customer recoveries. The hunter's +47% to +67% sits inside that published bracket. And the input is management's own disclosure on the call - ~$19M of the ~$23M revenue-recognised recoveries flowed to adjusted EBITDA - not something dug out of the exhibit. I verified the rest of the arithmetic and it is all correct: Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.1% on $233.7M net sales, so $7.3M; $26.9M less ~$19M is $7.9M on $275.6M underlying, i.e. 2.9%, flat with Q3; FY26 $68.2M less $19M is $49.2M. Correct, material, and already in the sell-side's own framing of the guide. The company itself appears to have presented the ex-recoveries comparison in the Q4 deck, which makes this the definition of restating published guidance. What is not priced is a narrower question - whether Q1 specifically shows the first instalment of that ~50-60% ramp - but that is a forecast, not a finding.

findings.finding: The +16.5% five-session run-up happened entirely AFTER the only piece of news: Craig-Hallum's initiation moved the stock +14.9% on 2026-08-25 to $16.05, and it then closed up four straight sessions (~17.06, 17.78, 18.23, 18.32, 18.705) on rising volume with no company release in that window other than the 26 Aug earnings-date notice - leaving spot above Baird's $16 target and at 86% of the $22 average target going into a quarter the company guided to be the seasonally weak one.
findings.adversary_note: This finding is the baseline. run_up_5d_pct is 16.54 and run_up_20d_pct is 23.87 in the sealed file; the Craig-Hallum move is the hunter's own cited StockStory/FinancialContent article of 2026-08-25; the price targets ($16 low, $22 average, $30 high) are on stockanalysis' public forecast page; and 'the company guided Q1 to be seasonally weak' is the CFO's own sentence from 2026-06-24. Every element is either in the sealed baseline the hunters were handed or on a public quote page. I did verify the structural observation and it holds - 5 sessions back from the 18.705 close is exactly the 2026-08-25 close of $16.05, so the 16.5% run-up is indeed entirely post-initiation, and I found no company release in the window other than the 26 August date notice. But an unexplained momentum run-up into a guided-weak print is the most legible setup on a screen, and the option market has already responded to it: the ATM IV is 106.5% and the 25-delta put skew is +14.23 vol points with the baseline itself labelling the priced direction 'downside paid'. Two small corrections: the initiation day's close-to-close move was +14.40% (Yahoo: $14.03 to $16.05), the +14.9% being intraday; and the $22 average target is stale against Craig-Hallum's $30, which is now the high end of a $16-$30 range.

findings.finding: SemiAnalysis's deep supply-chain teardown of the 800VDC rack transition does not mention Methode Electronics anywhere, and names TE Connectivity for the standardized busbars in the Diablo 400 specification alongside Delta, ABB, Legrand and EAE for 800VDC distribution.
findings.adversary_note: I verified the claim and it is factually correct: the SemiAnalysis 800VDC piece of 2026-05-26 does not mention Methode Electronics and does name TE Connectivity for the standardized busbars in the Diablo 400 specification. But the mechanism does not reach tonight's print, and that is the whole problem. 800VDC is not in FY27 guidance by management's own explicit statement on 2026-06-24 - 'none of that is in our guide' - so no Q1 FY27 revenue line, no FY27 guide component, and no consensus number moves on it. Nor does the piece contradict what the market is actually paying for: the $80M-to-$130M datacentre ramp is existing vendor-managed busbar volume with hyperscalers moving from spot buys to multi-week EDI, which is a different business from being a named supplier in an OCP rack specification, and TE being named for Diablo 400 busbars does not exclude Methode from other hyperscaler programs. Publication-wise this is genuinely awkward to score: SemiAnalysis is a paid newsletter, so it is not wire copy, but it is the single most-read AI-supply-chain publication among exactly the specialist holders who bid this stock from $14.03 to $18.705, and the piece predates the June guide by a month and the Craig-Hallum initiation by three. The specialists read it and initiated at $30 anyway. What is unpublished is the specific juxtaposition - MEI's 800VDC option value versus its absence from the teardown - and I found nobody drawing it. That is worth a middling number, capped hard by the fact that the only channel to tonight's outcome is whether management oversells 800VDC on tomorrow morning's call.

findings.finding: The Q2 FY27 consensus of $2.68 EPS / $297.8M revenue has been unchanged for 60 days - i.e. it was never re-based after Q1 printed $3.24 vs $1.82 (+78%) and $291.0M vs $249.4M (+16.7%) - and it implies revenue up only 2.3% sequentially and EPS down 17% sequentially in Argan's seasonally strongest construction quarter, while the same analysts' FY27 annual estimate ($1.28B revenue, $12.09 EPS, 5 analysts, as of 2026-08-26) requires ~$330M and ~$2.95 per quarter across Q2-Q4.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is in wire copy, and the finding's own source is the wire copy: the Zacks piece syndicated on Yahoo on 2026-09-01 states the $2.68 EPS consensus 'has remained unchanged over the past 60 days' and the $297.8M revenue figure, one day before the print. The Q1 surprise magnitudes are also published verbatim — Investing.com's 2026-06-04 transcript headline is literally 'Argan's Q1 2027 earnings surpass forecasts with 78% EPS surprise', which is the $3.24 vs $1.82 in this finding. The FY27 $1.28B / $12.09 aggregate is a public consensus screen. What is genuinely un-drawn is only the bridge (annual implies ~$330M/~$2.95 per quarter vs a Q2 stub of $297.8M/$2.68), and that bridge mixes a Zacks quarterly consensus with a 5-analyst annual from a different aggregator, which is exactly how unrevised quarterly splits behave on a lumpy EPC name. Two further problems: the premise that Q2 is 'Argan's seasonally strongest construction quarter' is wrong — FY26 went Q1 $193.7M, Q2 $237.7M, Q3 $251.2M, so Q3 is the seasonal peak and a modest Q1-to-Q2 step is not anomalous. And the mechanism is directly falsified by this name's own most recent reaction: on 2026-06-04 Argan beat by 78% on EPS and 16.7% on revenue and the stock moved +0.77%. A 15.7% option-implied move also says nobody is treating $2.68 as a tight anchor.

findings.finding: Short interest is 1.02M shares - 7.38% of float and 3.28 days to cover as of the 2026-09-02 data date - on only 14.02M shares outstanding, and days-to-cover is up 65% year over year; the position was built during a 33% 20-day drawdown that the only article addressing it attributes entirely to a sector reassessment with no Argan-specific news.
findings.adversary_note: Short interest is a semi-monthly public exchange release, republished by every screen including the finding's own source, and Benzinga runs a standing 'Looking Into Argan's Recent Short Interest' series on this exact ticker. The level is not an outlier: Benzinga puts the AGX peer-group average at 6.27% of float against AGX's 6.5-7.4%, so this is a peer-typical position, and 3.28 days to cover on ~277k shares of average daily volume is trivially coverable — not squeeze fuel. The 65% year-over-year rise in days-to-cover is as much a volume-denominator artifact as a positioning statement. Most damaging, the claim's direction is undefined: the same fact is offered as informed bearish positioning and as squeeze kindling, and the baseline's own positioning read cuts against the bearish version — put/call open interest is 0.31, i.e. the listed book is call-heavy, and 25-delta put skew is only 2.63 vol points, a mild rather than an alarmed downside bid. This is the textbook 'structural and known' case: real, public, and not worth much either way against a 15.7% implied move.

findings.finding: In a Q1 10-Q footnote, contract liabilities (customer billings and advances ahead of cost) rose to $565.8M at 2026-04-30 from $514.0M at 2026-01-31 while $222.6M of revenue was recognised out of that balance - implying roughly $274M of fresh customer cash advanced in a quarter that recognised $291M of revenue, against contract assets of only $36.9M.
findings.adversary_note: The headline balance is not a buried footnote — contract liabilities of $565.774M at 2026-04-30 versus $513.969M at 2026-01-31 appear in the 2026-06-04 earnings release exhibit itself, and the cash consequence was the release's second headline (total cash and investments $973.6M versus $895.0M, net liquidity $421.4M, no debt). The customer-funded working-capital structure of Gemma's large gas EPC contracts is the best-known single feature of the AGX story and the reason the company carries roughly a billion of cash; every bull note recites it. What is genuinely 10-Q-only and un-drawn anywhere I could find is the roll-forward decomposition — $222.6M recognised out of the opening balance, hence ~$274M of fresh advances — and the $36.9M contract-asset offset. So I credit real obscurity on the arithmetic and none on the fact. Against that: it is a Q1 datum, three months old, filed 2026-07-02, and it will be superseded within hours by the Q2 balance sheet. As a forward read it says Argan is billing ahead of cost on projects entering peak construction, which is the same thing the Q1 revenue beat already said and which the market answered with +0.77%.

findings.finding: Backlog has now declined for two straight quarters from its peak - RUPO of $3.0B at 2026-10-31 per the Q3 10-Q, $2.9B at 2026-01-31, $2.8B at 2026-04-30 - and Argan has press-released and 8-K'd zero new power EPC awards in the three months since the Q1 call, the only 8-K being an $8.3M teledata bolt-on (ValCor, 2026-08-04), against management's Q1 guidance of 'a handful of new projects over the next 10 to 18 months' and add-on backlog additions of only ~$125M in Q1; on ~$320-350M of Q2 revenue that makes a third consecutive sequential decline to roughly $2.6-2.7B the likely headline.
findings.adversary_note: I verified the absence-of-filings claim directly and it is factually correct — EDGAR shows only five 8-Ks in 2026 (2026-03-26 item 2.02, 2026-04-08 items 8.01/9.01, 2026-06-04 item 2.02, 2026-06-10 items 5.07/8.01, 2026-08-04 items 8.01/9.01 = the $8.3M ValCor teledata bolt-on), so no power-EPC award has been announced since 2026-04-08, and no award press release exists in the window either. The backlog series is also correct ($3.0B at 2025-10-31, $2.929B at 2026-01-31, $2.767B at 2026-04-30 — the finding's '2026-10-31' is a typo for 2025-10-31). But every one of those points was a press-release headline, and the decline plus its interpretation has been published and traded: Quiver ran 'Argan Falls as Investors Weigh Insider Selling and a Small Backlog Pullback' on 2026-07-02 on a day the stock fell 7.3%, quoting 'near-term order momentum' concerns; Zacks has since written that 'backlog declined from $2.93 billion to $2.77 billion as existing projects progressed faster than new awards were announced'; and the ratings followed — Zacks Research cut to Hold on 2026-08-07, Weiss to B- on 2026-08-11, Wall Street Zen to Hold mid-August. Meanwhile the tape is -33.22% over 20 days and -48.35% from the 52-week high. There is also a logical hole the finding concedes against itself: Q1 added roughly $125M of backlog with no 8-K at all, so zero award 8-Ks is weak evidence of zero bookings, and the third-consecutive-decline number depends on a Q2 revenue figure the finding gets from the bullish sibling claim. I still rate this the least-priced of the six: the specific arithmetic landing at $2.4-2.7B is unpublished, and backlog is demonstrably the variable this stock trades on.

findings.finding: Two state-level restrictions on data-center grid interconnection landed after Argan last spoke to investors on 2026-06-04 - Abbott ordered PUCT/ERCOT to audit data centers before approving new connections and ERCOT paused its 'batch zero' review (2026-08-03), and Pennsylvania restricted data-center permitting (2026-08-18, on which Talen fell 11%) - but the Texas order explicitly exempts data centers with on-site power generation, which is precisely the dedicated behind-the-meter gas plant Gemma builds.
findings.adversary_note: Both legs and the supposed twist are all in mainstream wire copy, and the twist has been in headlines. The Abbott directive was covered on the day by the Texas Tribune (the finding's own source), Houston Public Media and Utility Dive, then by Forbes on 2026-08-06 and again on 2026-08-12 under 'Data Center Moratoriums And The Rise Of Private Grids', and by client alerts from Gibson Dunn, Holland & Knight and Troutman Pepper Locke — all of which state that the audit does not reach behind-the-meter projects that do not intend to connect to ERCOT, naming Fermi and Pacifico's on-site gas-turbine projects. Bisnow's headline was 'Texas Pauses Data Center Power Connections, Which Could Speed Up Rapid Development'. On the Pennsylvania side, Utility Dive's headline on the Shapiro order was literally 'Pennsylvania dangles permitting carrot for data centers that bring their own power', syndicated further. So the exemption for on-site generation is not an obscure detail a hunter surfaced; it is the framing several outlets chose. The only unpublished step is naming Argan as the beneficiary, and even that is the oldest part of the AGX bull case. Price evidence is strong: the 20-day window over which the stock lost 33.22% starts right at the 2026-08-03 Abbott order, so the market has already traded this policy set — including whatever offset it believes the exemption provides. Mechanism also only reaches the print through call commentary, not through any reported Q2 number.

findings.finding: Director John R. Jeffrey Jr. sold 5,716 shares at an average $579.64 on 2026-07-31, cutting his direct holding to 2,533 shares - roughly a 69% reduction of direct ownership, executed within 4% of the 52-week high and 41% above the current $412 spot.
findings.adversary_note: This was in the wire copy the day the Form 4 hit. MarketBeat published 'Insider Selling: Argan (NYSE:AGX) Director Sells $3,313,222.24 in Stock' on 2026-08-04 carrying the exact 5,716 shares, the $579.64 average, the 2,533 remaining direct shares and the 69.29% reduction figure this finding reports; StockTitan carries the filing page as well. Insider selling at AGX is also a months-old, thoroughly published theme rather than a new datum: Quiver on 2026-07-02 documented 31 insider trades over six months, all sales, zero purchases, roughly $108M disposed, including the non-executive chairman's 30,000 and 20,000 share sales in June, on a day the stock fell 7.3%; Sahm Capital wrote up an independent director selling 28% of their holding back on 2026-04-07. The 69% figure is also overstated as a statement about ownership: I read the Form 4 and it discloses 8,000 shares held indirectly in 'John R. Jeffrey, IRA', so total beneficial holding went from 16,249 to 10,533, a 35% reduction, not 69%. And the size is immaterial — $3.3M by one non-employee director against a roughly $5.8B market capitalisation, preceded by a Form 144 filed 2026-07-31, which is the signature of a pre-announced routine sale rather than a signal. The 'executed within 4% of the 52-week high' observation is true of essentially every insider sale that happens near a top and carries no information about the print.

findings.finding: FPDS-NG shows ZERO federal contract actions under 'C3.AI, INC.' signed between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-02, against 3 actions in Aug 2025 (~$4.38M: $150.5k MDA 8/8, $0 USAF 8/18, $4.231M Army 8/27) and 3 in Aug 2024 - a break in the pattern in the month agencies obligate ahead of the 30 Sept federal year end, and the reported quarter itself contained only three actions, one of which was a 2026-07-03 DOE modification captioned 'DEOBLIGATE FUNDING AND DESCOPE REMAINING WORK' (-$625,000).
findings.source_date: 2026-09-02 (live query; comparison windows retrieved from the same feed at https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=VENDOR_FULL_NAME%3A%22C3.AI%2C+INC.%22+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2025%2F08%2F01%2C2025%2F09%2F30%5D&sortBy=SIGNED_DATE&desc=Y)
findings.adversary_note: The datum is real and I could not find it published anywhere — I re-ran the query and confirm zero entries for VENDOR_FULL_NAME 'C3.AI, INC.' signed 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-02, and zero under a loosened VENDOR_NAME:'C3' scan for 2026-07-01 onward, so it is not a name-variant artifact. But four things drain almost all the value out of it. (1) Reach: 1 Aug – 2 Sep 2026 sits in fiscal Q2 FY27, not in the quarter being reported (1 May – 31 Jul 2026). It can only touch tonight's print through forward commentary. (2) The hunter's in-quarter framing is selectively wrong. The reported quarter's three actions are not 'one of which was a deobligation' in any meaningful sense: they include a NEW $14,125,000 MDA Other Transaction Agreement (HQ0860269E011, C3 AI-DLA prototype) signed 2026-05-05 — the single largest new C3 obligation of FY2026 — against a $625k DOE descope. Net in-quarter FPDS flow is roughly +$13.5M, i.e. the opposite sign to the claim's tone. (3) Magnitude: the Aug-2025 comparison base is $4.38M of obligations, of which $4.231M is one lumpy Army action and the rest is $150.5k plus a $0 mod. Against FY27 revenue guidance of $210–240M that is under 2% of revenue in *obligations*, which recognise over years, and the comparison rests on n=2 prior Augusts. August is also not the federal year-end obligation month — September is — so the 'ahead of 30 Sept' premise is the wrong month. (4) A sector-wide explanation is already documented: the FY2026 continuing resolution barred DoD from new-start R&D and production-rate increases, and GAO found 36 of 74 DoD programs reporting CR-driven schedule delays in 2026. Separately, FPDS under-counts C3 structurally — C3 sells through Carahsoft's GSA MAS (47QSWA18D008F), where the FPDS vendor is Carahsoft, and through prime integrators such as ECS on the Army intelligence work, where the FPDS vendor is ECS. C3's total direct FPDS obligations for all of FY2026 are about $30.2M against ~$250M of revenue and management's stated ~45%-of-bookings federal/defense/aerospace mix, so the feed sees a minority of the federal business and its month-to-month variance is mostly noise. Finally the conclusion the datum points at — C3's federal execution is impaired — is already the consensus and already in the price: C3 AI Federal was reorganised inside the restructuring that took headcount from ~1,075 to ~700, an analyst asked directly on the 3 June call how that restructuring hit the $450M Air Force ramp, the stock is 46% off its 52-week high, D.A. Davidson carries Underperform at $7 into tonight, and the 25-delta skew is +18.98 vol points with the baseline reading 'downside paid'. New number, consensus inference, immaterial size, wrong quarter.

findings.finding: C3's own Greenhouse ATS lists 67 open roles of which 11 are federal/defense-titled or Tysons, Virginia-based, including a newly created 'Senior Director, Product Management - C3 AI Defense and Intelligence', a 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions - Intelligence Community', 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions, Navy and Maritime Industrial Base', a dedicated 'Senior/Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Federal', and - the concrete tell - a second 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' posting based in Tysons, Virginia; 5 of the 9 quota-facing 'Strategic Solutions' openings are defense or intelligence specific, and 13 postings are Palantir-style 'Forward Deployed Engineer'/'Director, Forward Deployed Engineering' roles across New York, Chicago, Atlanta, Houston, London, Redwood City and Tysons.
findings.adversary_note: I pulled the same Greenhouse board and the counts broadly check out — 67 open roles, twelve federal/defense/intelligence-titled or Tysons-based, and yes, a second 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' in Tysons, Virginia. What does not check out is the novelty, and the per-posting dates are exactly the false-positive mode the brief flagged. The 'Senior Director, Product Management - C3 AI Defense and Intelligence' the claim calls 'newly created' was first published 2026-03-10 — nearly six months old, live before the reported quarter even began and before the 3 June print repriced the name. 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions - Federal Defense Sector' was first published 2023-05-24, over three years ago; 'Data Scientist (Federal)' 2025-09-18; 'Senior Corporate Counsel - Federal' 2025-09-10; 'Senior/Lead SRE – Federal' 2025-10-03; 'Navy and Maritime Industrial Base' 2026-03-23. Only four of the twelve postdate the last print, and the requisition open since May 2023 is either evergreen boilerplate or a role nobody has managed to fill — both the opposite of a funding tell. The claim's direction is also contradicted by the company's own numbers: the 3 June call disclosed headcount going from ~1,075 in January 2026 to about 700 with ~$135M of annualised cost reduction, and third-party posting trackers show 75 C3 listings in August 2026 against the 67 live today, so the req count is shrinking. Sixty-seven openings at a company that just cut 375 people is backfill inside an announced restructuring, not expansion, and 'funded' is an inference a job board cannot support — FY27 guidance already embeds a $(128)–$(160)M non-GAAP operating loss, so this spend is inside guidance rather than incremental to it. Above all, the conclusion is the published bull case, not a discovery: federal/defense/aerospace bookings +89% y/y at ~45% of total bookings was disclosed and written up in February 2026, the $450M Air Force RSO ceiling and the $500M DoD OTA are company press releases, FedRAMP Moderate was covered in January 2026, and the Defense and Intelligence Suite has its own product page. The board itself is a public careers page mirrored on Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn and levels.fyi. This is agreement with the consensus long thesis dressed as a data pull.

findings.finding: The DEF 14A filed 2026-08-28 discloses that Condoleezza Rice, a director since 2009 and the company's most prominent Washington name, is not standing for re-election, and that Jim Hagemann Snabe is on a leave of absence from the board and also not standing - eleven weeks after C3 issued a press release celebrating Snabe's appointment as European Commission Special Envoy for Industrial AI - while the replacement director appointed 2026-08-25 with a $900,000 option grant, John C. Dwyer, is a high-stakes litigation partner at Cooley from 1998 to 2023 and a former Acting Associate Attorney General, seated alongside a brand-new General Counsel granted 826,901 RSUs effective 2026-07-30.
findings.adversary_note: Three of the four legs of this composite were published by the company itself, two of them in dedicated press releases, and the fourth has no mechanical path to a revenue print. Snabe's leave of absence — and therefore his not standing — was announced in a C3 press release on 2026-06-22, filed as an 8-K on 2026-06-24 (items 5.02/7.01/9.01), picked up by TradingView and StockTitan and analysed by Simply Wall St; the proxy's 'not standing' language is the mechanical consequence of a leave the company itself publicised, so the hunter's 'eleven weeks after C3 celebrated Snabe's appointment' irony is a juxtaposition of two facts C3 volunteered. Dwyer's appointment and the exact $900,000 initial option award vesting over five years are in the 8-K filed 2026-08-25 and were written up in a Yahoo/Simply Wall St piece on 2026-08-31, which explicitly judged the appointment 'incremental rather than a major shift' next to the consumption-pricing transition. The new General Counsel's 826,901 RSUs effective 2026-07-30 were the subject of a Businesswire press release on 2026-08-04 and covered by StockTitan and others — that is wire copy, naming Tom MacMitchell and the vesting schedule. What is genuinely un-picked-up is Rice: I searched repeatedly and found no press coverage of her not standing for re-election, only the DEF 14A itself filed 2026-08-27 with no accompanying 8-K. So there is one obscure-but-public leg here, and I would score that leg alone around 35. Against that, the mechanism does not reach tonight's print at all: a Class III director retiring at 70 after seventeen years on a board that is being deliberately shrunk from twelve seats to eleven is a governance datum, not a revenue, bookings or guidance datum, and nothing about it lands inside the quarter ended 31 July 2026. The reading that a Cooley litigation partner and former Acting Associate Attorney General plus a new GC equals legal battening-down is inference layered on published facts, and the tape has been up 7.7% over the five sessions spanning both the proxy and the 8-31 write-up — the market saw this and bought.

findings.finding: US Mint American Eagle silver bullion sales in Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (Apr/May/Jun 2026) were 380,500 / 0 / 260,000 coins = 640,500, down 76% from the year-ago quarter's 2,620,000 (1,530,000 / 775,000 / 315,000) and down 92% from Q3 FY26's 8,180,000, with May 2026 the first calendar month of zero bullion Silver Eagle sales in the program's 40-year history - and Gold.com is both a Mint Authorized Purchaser and, since consolidating Sunshine Minting on 2026-04-02, the owner of the Mint's primary silver blank supplier.
findings.source_date: 2026 (May-2026 data month; date verified independently - see independence)
findings.adversary_note: The underlying data is an official, free, monthly-updated US Mint dataset (bullion-american-eagle-silver.csv), and the specific 'zero in May 2026, first full month in the program's history' headline was published on at least two bullion trade sites and folded into the routine CoinNews monthly sales coverage, with the May figure public in early June and the June figure in early July. My own arithmetic check against the published 'roughly 8.8 million ounces YTD through June, ahead of 2025 thanks entirely to a big January' confirms the hunter's monthly splits exactly (8.18M in Jan-Mar plus 380.5k + 0 + 260k = 8.82M), which also means the reconciliation is already sitting in public copy. Critically, the price moved on this story while it was happening: GOLD hit its 52-week high of $66.70 on 2026-02-09 and traded down to a $37.01 low in July, a 44% drawdown that maps almost exactly onto the five-month decline in Eagle orders and the premium collapse. Against that, Silver Eagle bullion is a proxy rather than a P&L line for this company - all Authorized Purchasers together took 8.18M coins in fiscal Q3 while Gold.com alone sold 34.6M ounces of silver that quarter, so the company's own Eagle exposure is single-digit percent of its silver ounces. What I do concede is genuinely new: nobody has published the link from zero Mint bullion orders to Sunshine Minting's silver-blank business, which Gold.com only consolidated on 2026-04-02 and which therefore carries a full quarter of cost against a customer that ordered nothing in May.

findings.finding: The retail premium over spot on 1oz American Silver Eagles - which is Gold.com's actual revenue per ounce, not the metal price - peaked at 19.16% on 2026-02-17 inside fiscal Q3, then fell to a 5.30% low on 2026-04-24, 6.69% on 2026-05-25 and a ~7.93% June average across fiscal Q4, and has kept falling in the current quarter: 8.48% average in July 2026 against 6.87% in August 2026.
findings.adversary_note: This is the best mechanism in the set - premium over spot times ounces really is this company's gross profit, not the metal price - and the specific magnitude (19.16% peak on 2026-02-17 collapsing to a 5.30% trough on 2026-04-24) is not drawn out anywhere I could find. But premium compression as the driver of A-Mark/Gold.com margins is a long-established, management-narrated theme rather than a discovery: the company's own fiscal Q1 2026 release described 'subdued demand and historically tight premium spreads', Northland previously downgraded the stock explicitly on 'softened demand, premium compression, and elevated gold and silver prices', and on the 2026-05-06 call Greg Roberts told the market directly that premiums had 'normalized' from the January-February extreme and that volume had 'retreat[ed] from where we were in January and February'. So the direction, the mechanism and management's own framing were all on the tape four months ago, and the sell-side responded by cutting the June-quarter estimate to $0.94-0.96 against Q3's $2.09 - a 55% sequential decline already embedded in the number. The premium series itself lives on a niche retail price-tracking site but is trivially observable to anyone who looks at a dealer page, which is what makes it 'published somewhere obscure' rather than private. The part of the claim that runs into July and August 2026 does not reach this print at all - that is fiscal Q1 2027 - and it directly contradicts GOLD-2#2's reading of the same July data.

findings.finding: Third-party e-commerce estimates put jmbullion.com revenue at $66.4M in July 2026 and down 24% over the trailing three months versus the preceding three months, while Similarweb's July 2026 data shows the site's global rank deteriorating from 18,648 to 20,259 over three months and traffic down 3% month-on-month.
findings.adversary_note: This is the one finding here that is genuinely obscure - a B2B e-commerce intelligence vendor page, not a financial publication, and I found no financial-press pickup of it. I will not pretend it is priced. What I will attack is whether it matters. First, the reliability: Grips puts jmbullion.com at $716.5M of 2025 revenue, which is an order of magnitude below the scale implied by Gold.com's actual DTC segment (JM Bullion alone was 27% of a $176.6M consolidated gross profit quarter), so this is a web-traffic-modelled figure with a large and unknown error term, and the Similarweb rank data it is paired with is free and public to anyone. Second, the window: the stated data period is July 2026, which is fiscal Q1 2027, not the quarter being reported, and the 'trailing three months versus preceding three months' comparison spans May-July against February-April, so only two of the three months sit inside fiscal Q4. Third, the mechanism: for a bullion dealer, revenue is metal price times ounces, and a 24% revenue decline into a period of sharply higher silver spot tells you about volume but says almost nothing about gross profit, which is set by premium. A 3% month-on-month traffic dip and a global-rank move from 18,648 to 20,259 is noise at this company's scale.

findings.finding: The company's own nine-month numbers imply extreme operating leverage that makes the lone $0.96 Q4 estimate fragile: 9M gross profit $342.8M less Q3's $176.6M leaves $166.2M for H1, and 9M net income $70.2M less Q3's $59.5M leaves just $10.7M - so at an H1-like ~$83M quarterly gross profit the business earns roughly $0.19 a quarter, against a Q4 cost base now carrying Q3's $78M SG&A plus a full quarter of consolidated Sunshine Minting and $19M+ of quarterly interest.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is in the company's own press release of 2026-05-06 - 9M gross profit $342.8M, Q3 $176.6M, 9M net income $70.2M, Q3 $59.5M, Q3 SG&A $78.0M, Q3 interest $19.0M - and I verified all six against the release itself. The derived H1 figures are two subtractions on numbers that were covered the same day by Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha, Globe and Mail and StockTitan, and the 9M diluted EPS of $2.65 against Q3's $2.09 puts the whole H1 EPS at $0.56 in the release's own summary table, so the 'H1 was nearly nothing' point is legible from the headline EPS line without any arithmetic at all. The Sunshine cost base was announced by GlobeNewswire on 2026-04-02. Most damaging: the exact framing this finding claims as its edge - that Q3 may have been an unrepeatable spike and the estimate is fragile - is in wire copy published today, before the print, by Investing.com: investors will scrutinise 'whether last quarter's performance represents a sustainable baseline or an opportunistic spike that will prove difficult to replicate.' And the 'lone estimate' argument cuts against the hunter, not for them: one or two estimates on a $1.27B-cap name with 71% ATM implied vol and an 8.87% event-implied move means nobody is anchored on $0.94 tightly enough for a miss to be a surprise. I do concede that no published source has put a specific number on the downside case, and $0.19 versus $0.94 would be a large miss - which is why this is 78 and not 90.

findings.finding: Global bar-and-coin gold demand fell 36% sequentially to 307.1t in calendar Q2 2026 from 476.8t in Q1 -- and those are precisely the two quarters that map to Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (the quarter being reported, one estimate at $0.96) and fiscal Q3 (which printed $2.09), while retail premium spreads simultaneously troughed at multi-year lows and US Mint Silver Eagle bullion orders from Authorized Purchasers, of which A-Mark is one, hit exactly zero in May 2026.
findings.adversary_note: This is the World Gold Council's flagship quarterly publication, released 2026-07-30 and picked up by Coin World and Seeking Alpha among others; Gold Demand Trends is the single most-read demand dataset in the sector and its numbers are in every gold desk's note within a day. Worse for the finding, the WGC's own framing of the same 307.1t number is the opposite of the hunter's: it describes bar and coin investment as having 'held steady year-over-year at 307 tonnes', consistent with the 305t five-year quarterly average from Q4 2020 to Q3 2025, and explicitly reads it as 'a return to more typical levels of buying following two extraordinarily strong quarters'. The -36% sequential figure is arithmetically right but is the mirror image of a Q1 that the publisher itself calls extraordinary, so the magnitude is not merely contested - the primary source contests it. Global bar-and-coin tonnage is also a poor proxy for this company, which is a US wholesaler and DTC retailer whose margin is premium not tonnage, and the WGC publishes a separate US Focus report that would be the right cut. The remainder of the finding restates GOLD-1#0's Silver Eagle zero and GOLD-1#1's premium trough rather than adding to them.

findings.finding: The baseline's two-print reaction history is half contaminated: the +9.87% move attributed to the 2026-02-05 amc earnings release was in fact the same-evening 4:10pm ET announcement of a $150m Tether PIPE at $44.50 with a board seat, alongside EPS of only $0.46 -- leaving 2026-05-06 (+0.95% on a sequential EPS jump from $0.46 to $2.09) as the only clean earnings reaction this registrant has produced.
findings.adversary_note: The factual core is correct and I verified it independently: the 8-K exhibit for the Q2 FY2026 release (accession 0001193125-26-039858) reports diluted EPS of $0.46 on $6.477B revenue and net income of $11.6M, and the Tether release timestamped 2026-02-05 4:10pm EST discloses $150M at $44.50 for 3.371 million shares - roughly 12% of the company at an 11.9% discount to the 10-day VWAP - with the right to nominate a director. That two-event collision on one evening is real and the +9.87% is far more plausibly the PIPE than a $0.46 print. But both releases were in wire copy the same night and the following morning across GlobeNewswire, Yahoo Finance, Globe and Mail, Barchart, the Manila Times and Tether's own newsroom, so nothing here is undiscovered - this is a correction to a research artifact, and a market does not price a truncated CIK history. The inference the finding invites is also the part I would not accept: that this registrant produces small earnings reactions because the only 'clean' print moved +0.95%. The same operating business, same CIK, under the former name produced earnings-day moves of roughly -16%, -13% and +9% in the two years before the rename, including a 13% drop on the prior-year fiscal Q4 print. The rename on 2025-12-01 was cosmetic; the reaction distribution is not 1%. The option market agrees - 8.87% event-implied, 71% ATM IV - so if anything the finding's own conclusion is backwards, and its directional payload is zero either way.

findings.finding: Gold closed fiscal Q4 at $4,007.69 on 30 June 2026 and then rallied above $4,700 by 24 August -- its first move above $4,600 since 15 May -- before giving back 5.62% in the final week of August, and Silver Eagle premiums recovered from the 6.69% May trough to an 8.57% July average; so management reports a dead quarter into a rising, volatile one that resembles the regime that generated fiscal Q3's $2.09.
findings.adversary_note: The gold price is the most continuously observed number in this sector and the August 2026 rally was front-page: Bloomberg ran 'Gold Miners Rally 33% in August as Debasement Trade Drives Investor Demand' on 2026-09-01, gold gained about 9.4% in the month from near $4,000 to a $4,633 peak, and the late-August give-back to $4,429 by 2026-08-31 on a hawkish Warsh Jackson Hole message was equally well covered. GOLD's own tape traded both legs in real time: +11.85% in August to a $47.25 high, then the baseline's run_up_5d of -6.81% as gold rolled over. That is the price already moving on this information twice, in the right direction and roughly the right size - which is the definition of priced. The finding also has a mechanism problem: the quarter being reported is the dead one, so the bullish content rests entirely on management's forward commentary on the call, not on the print, and a 4:30pm ET call is a separate event from the 4:05pm release the baseline is scored against. Finally its premium datum is selectively cut - it cites an 8.57% July average as a recovery while GOLD-1#1, using the same series, records 8.48% in July and 6.87% in August, so on the more recent month the two hunters agree the trend is down and this finding simply stops before it.
